extracted.intended_audience: funders, research administrators, and researchers studying grant peer review reliability
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation of reliability and procedures in grant peer review panels, comparing panel discussion consensus scoring to aggregation (averaging) of independent reviewer scores for medical research grant proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers scored proposals on 'Scientific quality' as one of the standard medical-research grant dimensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a primary content dimension for scoring; no additional scoring guidance provided in the summary beyond its inclusion among other standard dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers scored proposals on 'Originality' as a standard dimension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured as a distinct criterion alongside scientific quality, methodology, importance, applicant qualifications, and overall recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology / feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers scored proposals on 'Methodology / feasibility' (i.e., rigor and practicability of the proposed methods).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as a key technical assessment dimension in grant review scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance of the research question
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers scored the 'Importance of the research question' as a dimension of proposal evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates relevance/potential impact of the proposed research question within medical/epidemiological contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers scored 'Applicant qualifications' (the competence and track record of investigators).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to judge whether the applicant team can credibly carry out the proposed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers provided an 'Overall recommendation' summarizing their judgment of the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as the synthesizing ordinal/score that often drives funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter-rater agreement (kappa)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreement measured using Cohen/weighted kappa; example result: post-discussion panel agreement κ = 0.23 (95% CI: 0.08–0.39), indicating slight-to-fair agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kappa is used as the primary reliability metric; study finds kappa values commonly fall in the ~0.2–0.4 range (a practical 'ceiling'). Use kappa with CIs to characterize reliability of scoring methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportion of large disagreements (>=2 points)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proportion of pairwise large differences (≥2 points on the scoring scale) between panels or scorers was measured as an outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported proportions: individual reviewer pair differences around 36–40%; panel discussion scores 26%; mean of two reviewer scores 14% (the lowest proportion, i.e., best at reducing extreme disagreements). Use this metric to assess how aggregation methods reduce extreme score divergence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation procedure (panel discussion vs averaging independent scores)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparison of post-discussion consensus panel scores versus simple averaging of independent pre-discussion reviewer scores to determine which yields higher reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study conclusion: panel discussion is no more reliable than averaging independent scores; averaging may outperform discussion in reducing extreme disagreements. Therefore, when designing evaluation procedures, consider whether costly panel meetings are justified if the primary goal is inter-rater reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-effectiveness of panel meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the resource costs of convening panels (time, travel, money) relative to any reliability gains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels are described as expensive and, per study findings, provide no reliability benefit over averaging; funders should weigh monetary and time costs against other potential benefits when deciding to convene panels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose-of-discussion beyond reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition that panel discussion may serve functions other than improving scoring reliability (e.g., training reviewers, identifying issues for program staff, providing feedback to applicants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if discussion does not enhance reliability, panels may be warranted for these other functions. Use these alternative benefits as explicit criteria when deciding whether to hold panels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric structure and dimension design
rubrics_metrics.description: The organization and content of the scoring rubric (which dimensions are included and how they are defined) influence outcomes and may matter more than the aggregation procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implication from the study: aggregation choice (panel vs averaging) matters less than the rubric structure; therefore, invest effort in designing clear, discriminating scoring dimensions and definitions to improve evaluation quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical benchmark of reliability ceiling
rubrics_metrics.description: Empirical observation that a 'hard kappa ceiling' for peer review reliability tends to lie around 0.2–0.4 across multiple systems and methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this benchmark to set realistic expectations about achievable inter-rater reliability in grant peer review and to interpret kappa values in context.
